taskDescription: Complete the crossword using key terms from MI5.1-5 | Musculoskeletal, Skin & Soft-Tissue Infections.

words.clue: Bacteria that cannot survive in oxygen and require devitalized tissue to proliferate
Gram-positive spore-forming anaerobic rods including agents of tetanus and gas gangrene
The phospholipase C enzyme (alpha toxin) produced by Clostridium perfringens that destroys cell membranes
A crackling or popping sensation felt in tissues due to gas production by anaerobic bacteria
Spasm of jaw muscles causing difficulty opening the mouth, an early sign of tetanus
Muscle tissue necrosis caused by Clostridium perfringens toxins in gas gangrene
A chemically inactivated bacterial toxin used to produce immunity without causing disease
Extreme arching backward of the head and trunk due to extensor muscle spasms in severe tetanus
A dormant bacterial structure that survives harsh conditions until germination occurs
The Clostridium species most commonly causing gas gangrene with characteristic box-car morphology
High-dose antibiotic used alongside surgical debridement in gas gangrene treatment
